newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares recover from lows.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares recover from lows.

text.p: Belgian shares had clawed back most of their earlier losses by late afternoon Friday after Wall Street started positively, but dealers expected the market to remain jumpy in the short term.

"From next week onwards investors will be already looking towards first half earnings in the U.S. and then Europe," one dealer said. "Expectations for the U.S. are too high, (while) for Europe we expect some positive surprises," he added.
In the shorter term the market is seen nervous ahead of next week's Federal Reserve FOMC policy making meeting, though few expect it to result in a rise in interest rates.
By 1420 GMT on Friday, the Bel-20 index of leading shares stood just 4.23 points or 0.18 percent lower at 2,370.58 after touching 2,354.80 earlier in the session.
Among the seven Bel-20 stocks to buck the downward trend was chemicals firm Solvay, up 1.21 percent or 250 francs at 20,950.
"We've seen a big seller in Solvay - he must have finished now," one dealer said.
Another noted the stock had come down from 23,000 francs at the beginning of the month, adding: "People think its bottoming out now."
Royale Belge rose 75 francs to 10,275 amid continued speculation that Dutch ING might be interested in buying the Belgian insurer.

Retailer Colruyt, meanwhile, fell 175 francs to 17,300. Dealers said although the company announced a 12-percent rise in group net profit on Thursday night, current earnings had disappointed, and there was also profit taking after the company had failed to give details on the future of its Dolmen Computer Applications unit. KB-Securities said it had nevertheless reiterated its "accumulate" recommendation of the stock.
